mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 0.5% month-over-month signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% MoM and the S&P 500 still produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points month-over-month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases by more than 0.3pp MoM and the S&P 500 still produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent decline in housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST declines for three consecutive months and the S&P 500 still produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases by more than 1% MoM and the S&P 500 still produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 2% quarter-over-quarter, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy in a slowing economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and GDPC1 QoQ growth < 2% and the S&P 500 still produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 month-over-month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS decreases by more than 100,000 MoM and the S&P 500 still produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases for three consecutive months and the S&P 500 still produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of observed periods.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) decreases by more than 0.25% in a month and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) remains stable (change within ±0.2% MoM), it indicates a dovish monetary policy without inflationary pressure, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases > 0.25% MoM and CPIAUCSL change within ±0.2%
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS decreases by more than 0.25% MoM and CPIAUCSL change is within ±0.2% MoM, and the S&P 500 still produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances.
